Department settings change how a whole department sees and handles its work. They deserve the same review as a dispatch procedure. Open the department menu, then department settings. We are using the fictional Firehouse 51 department that these controls are equally relevant to a mobile crisis service, a search team, a patrol company, a wildland contractor, or a plant response team. Begin by identifying the problem you want to solve. Is the roster showing stale availability?
Off-duty members receiving unwanted alerts is a module confusing members who do not use it. Make one deliberate change, save it, and check its effect before changing several related controls. The department name identifies this workspace. The time zone affects local time displays and scheduled work. Our training department uses central time. Use 24-hour time changes how supported screens display the clock. It does not create 24-hour staffing coverage.
The account owner identifies the managing account. Review ownership and administrative access in the personnel and security workflows. Disable auto-available controls the automatic behavior described on this screen, setting personnel status to available after an hour. In this lesson, we turn that automatic behavior off. This avoids treating the passage of time as evidence that a person has finished a long assignment. It also makes deliberate member updates and supervisor follow-up more important.

Modern notifications select supported modern notification behavior, including modern push sounds. It does not establish a valid device registration or prove delivery. Review every channel and consumer your department uses. Require password resets by email directs administrator initiated member resets through single-use recovery links
instead of an administrator selecting a member's password. Require security pin governs sensitive supported assistant and text actions. These are security decisions and the owning administrator needs to review recovery arrangements and member enrollment. We leave their existing values visible and discuss their impact without changing credentials. TTS language selects the application's voice prompt language. That setting is separate from the warm Lulu narration used in this training video. Under sorting, we choose
last name for personnel. Units and calls have their own order settings. This is useful when a dispatcher knows the member's surname and needs a predictable roster. The address section describes the department base or office. Our address is fictional. Default map center accepts decimal latitude and longitude. Explicit coordinates pin the starting point. Leaving both blank lets the system work out a center from the saved address. A department center is a map starting point, not a live unit location.
a patrol boundary or proof that a resource is present. A search team can use its base, a security company, its operational office, and an industrial team, its facility access point. For a contractor deployment, review whether the department center or an incident specific view is appropriate. Personnel staffing reset and personnel status reset are different controls. Staffing describes availability. Status describes current activity. Our example enables the daily staff
reset at 8 a.m. and selects unavailable as its target. Members then need to declare their availability after the reset. This can help a volunteer search department avoid relying on yesterday's availability or a wildland contractor require a fresh crew check. It can also disrupt a team working overnight if the time and target do not fit its procedures. The daily status reset remains off in this example. Consider extended searches, patrol assignments, mental health responses,
and plant incidents before automatically replacing a current activity status. When you create custom personnel staffing or status sets, revisit these target selections. The intended label must resolve to the current option. The staffing suppression section lets the department select staffing levels that should be muted by supported notification paths. We enable suppression and select unavailable. Review the interaction carefully. At the daily reset, members are marked unavailable and supported
notifications can suppress them until their staffing is updated. This reduces off-duty noise, but a stale staffing declaration can exclude the person you intended to reach. For security, the procedure might distinguish on-duty patrol from off-duty staff. A mobile response service might distinguish the scheduled response team from the broader roster. An industrial team might distinguish the current plant ERT from other employees. Verify the intended recipients and fallback procedures.

Investigate the owning screen and saved value first. Open department modules. These switches control supported module availability and navigation. Turning a module on
does not purchase its add-on, grant missing permissions, or configure an external provider. We turn Calendar off and save. The page confirms the module settings were saved, and Calendar disappears from the side menu. We then turn Calendar back on, save, and reopen it. The three original training events are still present, disabling the module did not delete those records. The screen also warns that propagation can differ across features, so review the screens and apps your department actually
uses. For your practice exercise, select one behavior, explain who it affects, save it in a training department, reopen it, and inspect the result. Document the responsible reviewer and an operational test for any effect this configuration check cannot prove.
